items.title: NewsNation-DDHQ poll: Democrats lead generic ballot 49-42, three weeks out
items.summary: A NewsNation/Decision Desk HQ poll conducted by TrueDot.ai, released Oct 13, finds Democrats leading Republicans 49% to 42% on the generic congressional ballot, with 8% undecided. Democrats also led 46-40 on which party has done more to earn voters' support.

items.title: Rasmussen: Democrats lead generic ballot 49-44, advantage widened 2 points in a week
items.summary: Rasmussen Reports' Oct 12 survey of likely voters has Democrats at 49% vs 44% for Republicans on the generic ballot, up from 47-44 last week — an 8-point swing against the GOP since before the 2024 elections. Independents favor Republicans 45-40; women back Democrats by 12 points while men prefer Republicans by 5.

items.title: DDHQ: Democrats have 76% chance of winning House; Trump favorability at 38/60
items.summary: Decision Desk HQ estimates Democrats have a 76% chance of taking the House. Its Oct 13 poll found Trump at 38% favorable vs 60% unfavorable; inflation (28%) and jobs/economy (20%) top voter concerns, immigration at 12%. 'You're basically out of time for much to change,' said DDHQ chief elections analyst Geoffrey Skelley.

items.title: Texas Senate: Talarico's lead over Paxton shrinks to 4 points (48-44) ahead of early voting
items.summary: A ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll released Oct 13 shows Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 48% to 44%, down from a 6-point lead in September. Talarico leads independents 60-30; Paxton holds rural Texas by 18 points. No Democrat has won a Texas Senate seat since 1988. Early voting starts Oct 19.

items.title: Quantus poll: Paxton 47.2%, Talarico 46.7% — Texas Senate effectively tied
items.summary: A Quantus Insights survey of 839 likely voters puts Republican Ken Paxton at 47.2% and Democrat James Talarico at 46.7%, inside the margin of error. Paxton led voters 65+ by 17 points and held a 5-point suburban edge; Talarico led among independents, women, younger, Black, Hispanic and urban voters. RealClearPolling's average still has Talarico up 48.1-45.1.

items.event_time_ist: Rally announced Oct 13; rally Oct 19, Wichita
items.title: Trump to rally in Wichita Oct 19 for Sen. Roger Marshall as Kansas race becomes a toss-up
items.summary: The RNC announced Oct 13 that Trump will hold a midterm rally in Wichita on Oct 19 for Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, who faces Democrat Adam Hamilton in a race several pollsters now rate a toss-up. 'We can't win this without his voters,' Marshall said. Trump has been blitzing red states — Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas — and heads to North Carolina after Wichita.

items.title: Trump rallies in Ohio for Sen. Jon Husted amid competitive race against Sherrod Brown
items.summary: Trump held a midterm rally in Youngstown, Ohio on Oct 12 for Republican Sen. Jon Husted, who faces Democrat Sherrod Brown; he had campaigned in Vandalia on Oct 3 for Husted and GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. The RealClearPolling average has Brown leading Husted 47.4-44.3.

items.title: Cook Political Report moves 18 House races toward Democrats; Dems need just 20% of toss-ups
items.summary: Cook's Oct 9 ratings shift moved 18 races toward Democrats — nine GOP incumbents (Miller-Meeks, Nunn, Fitzpatrick, Perry, Huizenga, Wittman, Hill, Spartz and others), five Democratic incumbents, and four open seats. Cook's most likely outcome: Democrats gain 9-19 seats (224-234 total) and need only 20% of the 21 toss-ups for a majority. The NRCC dismissed it: 'House races are won in the districts, one by one.'

items.title: Prediction markets: Democrats 91% for House, 64% for Senate; sweep the leading scenario
items.summary: As of Oct 13, Polymarket priced Democrats at 91% to win the House and 64% to take the Senate; Kalshi's balance-of-power market also lists a Democratic sweep as the leading outcome. Polymarket's individual Senate markets favor Democrats in Texas, Maine, Michigan, Alaska and Ohio, while Republicans are favored in Iowa (Ashley Hinson). Market prices reflect trading, not polling.

items.event_time_ist: Data as of 7 AM ET, Oct 13
items.title: Michigan: mail ballot requests up 20% vs 2022; 440,677 ballots already returned
items.summary: Michigan officials said 2,083,240 voters had requested mail ballots — up over 20% from the same point in 2022 — and 440,677 had returned them (6% of active registered voters), slightly above 2022's pace. Michigan's gubernatorial race (Democrat Jocelyn Benson vs Republican Rep. John James) is among the key contests.

items.title: New Mexico: 21,022 ballots cast in first week of early voting; Democrats lead 12,526 to 5,504
items.summary: New Mexico's Secretary of State reported 21,022 ballots cast through Oct 8 in the first week of early voting (began Oct 6). Democrats cast 12,526 early ballots vs 5,504 Republicans; 2,868 unaffiliated voters also voted. Expanded early voting runs Oct 17-31.

items.title: Texas governor: Democrat Gina Hinojosa edges Gov. Greg Abbott 48-47 in YouGov poll
items.summary: A YouGov poll of 3,625 likely voters found Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa leading Republican Gov. Greg Abbott 48% to 47%, inside the 3-point margin of error. Both Democrats lead among women, Hispanic voters and voters 18-44; Republicans hold non-college and white voters. Early voting starts Oct 19.
